title: 2026-12-18-foxglove-integrations-sprint-zero-intake
summary: Sprint-zero intake for Foxglove's Redwood deployment. Covered integration touchpoints (EMR connector, webhook flows), security requirements (SSO/SAML, KMS), deployment topology options (hosted vs private VPC), and initial success criteria for the onboarding project. Agreed next steps: send deployment diagram, security pack, and schedule a private-runtime deep dive and pilot acceptance criteria workshop.
action_items: Alex Moreno: Share internal deployment diagram + sample config (due 2026-12-21)
Jules Park: Prepare private runtime checklist and list of supported quant configs (due 2026-12-22)
Maya Chen: Share EMR schema and sample dataset extract (due 2026-12-23)
Luc Moreau: Provide primary legal contact and list of compliance docs required (due 2026-12-24)
Tanya Iqbal: Schedule pilot acceptance criteria workshop (due 2026-12-20)
next_steps: Send security pack (SOC2, ISO statements, audit log examples)
Set up 1:1 with Foxglove SRE for private VPC sizing and network review
Confirm datacenter region preference and retention limits
Kick off sprint-zero JIRA board and invite stakeholders
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-12-18 10:00 PT / 13:00 ET
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Jules Park (Redwood SE), Tanya Iqbal (CSM) — Maya Chen (Head of Integrations, Foxglove), Ravi Patel (SRE), Sofia Alvarez (Product), Luc Moreau (Legal), Mateo (Data Eng)
Links shared: onboarding-runbook.link, security-pack.pdf, sample-config.yaml (note: link text, file shared after call)

[00:00] Alex: ok hey everyone thanks for joining, um this is Alex from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account, we also have Jules our solutions engineer and Tanya the CSM. really appreciate you all making time for the sprint zero intake.
[00:14] Maya: hey thanks Alex, yeah excited to get started. quick note — i'm on a train so audio maybe patchy?
[00:20] Jules: no worries, we can repeat if anything drops out. quick agenda: collector points, security & compliance, deployment topology options, pilot success criteria and milestones.
[00:33] Ravi: great. from SRE side we care about VPC peering, private endpoints, and traffic egress, and also the KV cache persistence — uh forgive me, K-V cash — caching behavior under failover.
[00:45] Alex: good note, we'll go into our prefix/KV cache options and TTLs, and also how the runtime behaves on preemptible GPUs vs reserved.
[00:56] Sofia: for product, the big ask is EMR integration — we need the inference results tied back to patient records, so mapping and schema are important. we'll share a sample extract after this call.
[01:10] Jules: perfect, that helps. quick question Maya — do you expect the model requests to flow through a backend queuing layer or directly from the app?
[01:18] Maya: most will come from our backend mid-tier. a small percentage might be event-driven webhooks from triage flows. we expect bursty spikes at clinical shift changes, so autoscaling behavior and burst capacity matters.
[01:31] Alex: noted — Redwood Dedicated can reserve baseline throughput and allow burst to hosted when needed, or you can do a private deployment with explicit capacity. tradeoff is predictable latency vs. operational control.
[01:45] Luc: from legal — we need to confirm encryption at rest with customer-managed keys, and whether audit logs are exportable for our SOC2 audits. also data residency — european patients must remain in eu regions.
[01:58] Jules: yes we support CME-integrations — sorry that sounded weird, i mean key management integrations like KMS/HSM, and audit logs are accessible via the console and can be exported. we'll add the doc links.
[02:10] Mateo: small question on model updates — can we pin model versions per route? during clinical trials we want frozen model behavior.
[02:18] Alex: yes — you can pin model versions and rollouts are controlled via the console; canary or A/B rollouts are supported. we'll capture that in the runbook.
[02:26] Maya: timeline — we are targeting a Q1 pilot acceptance for our internal beta. is that realistic?
[02:33] Jules: seems reasonable. sprint-zero is about integration and security gating; then a 4-week pilot window. but it depends on connectivity and your sample dataset availability.
[02:44] Maya: we'll aim to hand over dataset and schema by end of next week.
[02:50] Alex: great. on the network side, Jules what do you recommend for initial topology?
[02:54] Jules: for a first pass we suggest hosted + private VPC peering for sensitive routes: keep core inference in Redwood-hosted for faster onboarding, then if you need full isolation move to Private deployment in your VPC. note: private has additional setup time — about 2-3 weeks for infra and certs.
[03:14] Ravi: 2-3 weeks is ok but need to plan for firewall rules and egress controls — will require our network team.
[03:21] Alex: we'll provide a network checklist. also want to call out telemetry — we can send token-level billing and latency breakdowns per route so you can monitor cost.
[03:33] Sofia: nice, can we get a heatmap for token consumption per EMR route?
[03:37] Jules: yes, per-route dashboards are available in the console. we'll show a sample during the pilot.
[03:44] Maya: security questions: SSO — we prefer SAML and want SCIM for automated provisioning.
[03:50] Tanya: we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning, and we can walk Luc through roles & RBAC mapping.
[03:58] Luc: one more legal ask: retention windows — is there a way to set short-term retention for PII-derived logs?
[04:05] Jules: you can configure retention at the workspace level; longer-term audit logs can be archived to your bucket. we'll include retention docs in the security pack.
[04:16] Mateo: about evaluation: during pilot we want to run side-by-side latency tests against our current system and Redwood. what's the best way?
[04:24] Jules: we can provide a benchmark harness and a hosted test workload; if you want private deployment benchmarks we can run a controlled load with your SRE involved.
[04:33] Ravi: perfect. also curious about model quantization — we might accept slight accuracy tradeoffs to reduce cost. what quant configs are supported?
[04:41] Jules: we have recommendations per model family; some support 4-bit and 8-bit quant; we'll send the quant recommendation sheet. note: quality monitoring can detect drift vs your eval sets.
[04:54] Alex: okay, let's talk risks and blockers quickly: network approvals and legal review are likely blockers — Luc anything to flag?
[05:02] Luc: we'll need indemnity language for PHI handling; our checklist will go to your legal. timeline may slip depending on redlines.
[05:10] Alex: understood — we'll have legal follow up.
[05:13] Maya: final thing — can Redwood guarantee no model training on our data?
[05:19] Jules: Redwood does not use customer prompt data to train public models. we can provide contractual language in the data processing addendum.
[05:25] Mateo: crosstalk — so for alerts we want escalation contacts, can we set up a 24/7 escalation path for pilot?
[05:31] Tanya: yes we'll work with you to set on-call rotation and runbook.
[05:34] Alex: ok wrapping up — quick recap of owners and due dates. (brief pause) Jules will send the private-runtime checklist, Alex to send deployment diagram and security pack, Maya to share dataset, Luc to give legal contact, Tanya to schedule the workshop.
[05:51] Maya: sounds good, thanks all.
[05:54] Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up by email with the links and next steps.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcript: transcription contains minor errors (speaker overlap and some product name mis-hearings), timestamps approximate.
